decision: list other sessions from Claude Code's session registry and port them in (option 1 of 3)
why: Manuel wants to see sessions started in Tabby, Termius, or as forks, and move them into orfoni over time; the registry needs no change to his global settings

decision: a registry entry appears within 5 s of a claude start with its pid, procStart, conversation, folder, name, status, and tmux pane
why: discovery and the pid reuse check depend on these fields

decision: SIGTERM ends a session in about 1.6 s, removes its registry file, keeps the transcript intact, and returns the pane to its shell; claude --resume=<id> appends to the same transcript
why: porting rests on a clean exit and a lossless resume
evidence: spike-port.sh run on a throwaway haiku session

decision: other sessions get no composer, approval cards, or terminal in orfoni, only their read-only chat and a Port button
why: sending and approvals need orfoni's hooks, and attaching to a pane in his tmux would disturb his Tabby layout

decision: porting refuses a busy session and one now on another conversation, ends the process with SIGTERM, waits up to 10 s, then resumes with the registry name as the orfoni title and no --name flag
why: a port mid-turn loses work; a /clear between list and port would resume the wrong conversation; --name would turn a derived name into a user-set one

decision: the registry is read every 5 s, a file that does not parse is skipped, and a missing folder means no other sessions
why: the registry is an internal Claude Code file, so a format change must empty the list and break nothing else

decision: porting refuses background sessions until a check has ended one from outside
why: a background session runs under Claude Code's daemon, which may start it again and leave two processes on one conversation

decision: the registry reader keeps only interactive and bg records and skips parked windows, spare processes, the daemon and its workers, and files not named after their pid
why: Claude Code registers those too, and porting one would end a process that is not the session shown
evidence: final review Important 2, verified by probe

decision: a port in progress is keyed by conversation, and a conversation open in more than one process is refused
why: two records on one conversation could start two orfoni sessions on it
evidence: final review Important 2, verified by probe

decision: a launch that fails after the old process ended keeps the conversation as an offline orfoni session; the timeout error names claude --resume=<id>
why: otherwise the conversation was in neither list
evidence: final review Important 1, verified by probe

decision: opening an outside session ends viewing the orfoni session open before

evidence: final review Important 4, verified by probe

decision: regraded Minor to Important: an outside session's chat reloads only when a turn ends
